findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

Raise: Security. The validation at this line accepts an event object with `"event": null` because it checks the field's type only when the value is non-null. When the board merges that PR record, `item()` calls `.startswith()` on the null value at time_records.py:84 and raises `AttributeError`. A PR author can therefore make `forge board` fail by editing the shared record. This is distinct from the dismissed null-row finding: the row is a dictionary, but its event type is null.
findings.title: Null event type in a pull request record crashes the board

findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

Raise: Test. The new GitHub stub wrapper replaces `sys.stdin` with `io.StringIO` after reading a merge body. The merge stub it wraps reads `sys.stdin.buffer` (tests/test_last_task_records_story_outcome.py:43), so each parameterized merge fails with `AttributeError` before the test can verify the submitted body. The supplied suite output records all five cases failing this way; the required command-level proof is red.
findings.title: Not done: the pull-request body-limit command test passes

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Raise: Security. `from_body` accepts any finite nonnegative duration, including `1e308`. A PR author can put that value in a review timing; `merged()` passes it to `item()`, where `timedelta(seconds=seconds)` raises `OverflowError`. Reading that PR then crashes `forge board` or `forge next`. This is a distinct case from the earlier malformed-row finding: the row passes the new type checks.
findings.title: A finite duration in a PR record can crash board and next

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Raise: Functional. On a repeat close that hits a default-branch conflict, this call publishes a fabricated `reviewing` result with no findings or evidence. `_publish` replaces the PR's managed block, so an existing blocked review loses its findings and proof list and appears to be running after close has stopped.
findings.title: A merge conflict replaces an existing PR's review and proof

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Raise: Functional. The board passes only part and read intervals plus the story start to `time_records.story`, then sets `unfinished=False` for a done story. That function extends a runway to now only when unfinished (time_records.py:485); it receives no completion bound. When a human records a story outcome after its last part merges, the intervening elapsed time is absent from the story's unknown seconds and total. The added runway test covers an unfinished story only.
findings.title: Completed stories omit elapsed time after their last part

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Item 12 remains incomplete in this branch: the board retains its old counts and card page, blocking plan problems are absent from Needs you, and the pane still formats abbreviated times. The pinned folding sections, story keys and cold-read history are also absent. The story assigns these behaviors to COUNTS, WAITS, NAV and PANE.
findings.title: Later: COUNTS, WAITS, NAV and PANE complete item 12
